---
title: Installation
---

velocirepo can be used as a GitHub Action for automated nightly fetching, or installed locally for ad-hoc use.

## GitHub Actions (recommended)

Generate the workflows (no installation required):

```bash
uvx velocirepo install-ci
```

It writes the nightly workflow, a heartbeat that checks it ran, and a weekly digest. The nightly workflow looks like this:

```yaml
name: Fetch Metrics

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '30 9 * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      release:
        description: "Land a project's held-back data: <source>/<project>"
        required: false
        default: ""
      discard:
        description: "Discard a project's held-back data: <source>/<project>"
        required: false
        default: ""
      repair:
        description: "Re-fetch or replay a range: <source>/<project> <from>..<to>"
        required: false
        default: ""

# One run at a time: a run that is in progress is allowed to finish.
concurrency:
  group: velocirepo-gate
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write  # commit the data, and store the archive as release assets
  issues: write    # the tracking issue
  actions: read    # archives saved as artifacts by earlier runs

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          # The history back to the last commit the gate checked.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: posit-dev/velocirepo@v1
        with:
          mode: gate
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GH_TOKEN }}
          plausible-token: ${{ secrets.PLAUSIBLE_TOKEN }}
          youtube-token: ${{ secrets.YOUTUBE_TOKEN }}
          release: ${{ inputs.release }}
          discard: ${{ inputs.discard }}
          repair: ${{ inputs.repair }}
          # Optional: a Healthchecks ping URL, for a heartbeat outside GitHub.
          healthchecks-url: ${{ secrets.HEALTHCHECKS_URL }}
```

The gate fetches, checks the night's changes, commits and pushes, and keeps a tracking issue; see [Keeping the data right](reliability.qmd). A failing source doesn't keep the other sources' data from being committed, while the run still shows the failure. Workflows generated by earlier versions, which run `velocirepo fetch` and commit in a shell step, keep working.

## Local installation

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)

```bash
brew install posit-dev/tap/velocirepo
```

### Scoop (Windows)

```powershell
scoop bucket add posit-dev https://github.com/posit-dev/scoop-bucket
scoop install velocirepo
```

### uv

```bash
uv tool install velocirepo
```

Or run without installing:

```bash
uvx velocirepo fetch
```

### Go

```bash
go install github.com/posit-dev/velocirepo/cmd/velocirepo@latest
```

### From source

```bash
git clone https://github.com/posit-dev/velocirepo.git
cd velocirepo
go build -o bin/velocirepo ./cmd/velocirepo
cp bin/velocirepo ~/.local/bin/
```

### Shell installer (macOS / Linux)

```bash
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posit-dev/velocirepo/main/install.sh | sh
```

This downloads the latest binary to `./bin/velocirepo`. Set `INSTALL_DIR` to install elsewhere:

```bash
curl -sSfL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/posit-dev/velocirepo/main/install.sh | INSTALL_DIR=/usr/local/bin sh
```

### Download binary

Pre-built binaries for Linux, macOS, and Windows are available on the [Releases](https://github.com/posit-dev/velocirepo/releases) page.

## Shell completion

```bash
# Zsh (add to ~/.zshrc)
eval "$(velocirepo completion zsh)"

# Bash (add to ~/.bashrc)
eval "$(velocirepo completion bash)"

# Fish
velocirepo completion fish | source
```
